clue.text: Detectives arresting a large number about driving

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the whole assembled string round to read the other way
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
many means a large number

explanation.surface: Police officers detain a crowd of people over a motoring offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the whole container, not just the detectives. 'driving' looks like a motoring charge but is the definition, as in a driving force.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving personality or force is energetic and forceful, which is what dynamic describes.

clue.text: Day getting behind instead of having a routine

indicators.note: getting says the day word acquires a new piece in place of a letter
instead of having a means the A of the day word is swapped for the new piece

parts.note: the word itself
rear means behind

explanation.surface: A day of falling behind with work rather than keeping to a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' after 'instead of having' is a letter in the clue's first word, not an article; 'routine' is used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means dull and unvarying, a close synonym of dreary.

clue.text: Regularly visited Andes via a drab desert area

indicators.note: regularly visited means only every other letter is called at, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A traveller in South America calls at the Andes and a dull stretch of desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andes' points to South America; the answer is a US state, much of it desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The American state lies largely within the Great Basin and Mojave, so it is mostly desert.

clue.text: Anthem is taken lyrically partly the wrong way

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A national song's words are partly misheard and sung wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mistakenly means doing it in error, the wrong way.

clue.text: Increase in clubs needing member's support

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A rise in golf clubs means the player's arm needs support.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb, as prices or figures do, is to rise or go up, so it is a verb of increase.

clue.text: Rejected cheque for unsafe delivery?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cheque the bank returns unpaid is said to bounce
second meaning: in cricket a ... is a short ball that rears up at the batter's head

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler 'delivers' the ball; a bouncer is a short-pitched ball aimed to rise at the batter, hence unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from bouncing: a dishonoured cheque bounces, and a cricket ball pitched short bounces up dangerously.

clue.text: Duck stuffing belongs to cook, to go with English sauce

indicators.note: to go with adds the next piece on at the end
stuffing means filling, so the zero goes inside the jumbled letters
to cook means to work over or doctor, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a stuffed duck with a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BELONGS, 'to cook', is BLOGNES; 'stuffing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolognese is an Italian meat-and-tomato sauce traditionally served with pasta.

clue.text: Strange visions of upsets coming between us

indicators.note: coming between means placed inside the letters of us
in a down clue upsets means turned upside down, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Odd apparitions arising from the quarrels that divide a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are strange sightings in the sky, hence odd visions.

clue.text: Party and gin fizzes after a promotion

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled spirit behind the article

parts.note: a camp is a party or faction holding a shared view

indicators.note: fizzes suggests bubbling up and stirring, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebration with sparkling cocktails after someone moves up a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertising or political campaign is an organised drive to publicise something, which is a promotion.

clue.text: Cowboys went galloping, with half-hearted applause

parts.note: ran means went fast, as at a gallop

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the pair of central letters is lost

parts.note: cheers are applause

explanation.surface: Cowboys rode off to a lukewarm response.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranchers run cattle ranches and so are, loosely, cowboys of the American West.

clue.text: Where we rank books without leading characters. 'Little Women' maybe …

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word for book storage are dropped

parts.note: books are stood in ranks on shelves

explanation.surface: A library note: shelving the books, then a nod to Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Women' is not the novel but small female folk; the ellipsis carries the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small folk of legend, so female ones could playfully be called little women.

clue.text: .. not welcome here?

parts.note: read on from the previous clue: little women would not be welcome on an island named for men

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue before: the island's name sounds as if only men belong, so women would not be welcome. It is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of this Irish Sea island jokingly implies a place reserved for males, where females are unwanted.

clue.text: Food delivered by hired cab — bag extra

indicators.note: delivered by says the answer is carried within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A takeaway brought by taxi, with a surcharge for the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-leaved variety of cabbage is a vegetable eaten pickled or braised, so it is a food.

clue.text: Walk in quiet city with abbey but no bishop

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: but no says a letter is removed from the city

parts.note: Bath is an English city with a famous abbey
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A stroll around a cathedral city, noting its abbey but no sign of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk can mean a footway or route for walking, which is what a path is.

clue.text: Trickery needed? Get Rufus and be tickled!

indicators.note: tickled suggests stirred up and played about with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A playful plan to make Rufus laugh by tickling him.
explanation.definitionFit: A subterfuge is a deceptive trick used to achieve an aim, so it is trickery.

clue.text: Bunny food?

parts.note: rabbits eat greens, so a rabbit-friendly patty would be a meat-free one

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a clue for carrots or lettuce; the hyphenated pattern points to a meat-free patty in a bun, playing on 'bunny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty made of vegetables and served in a bun suits a herbivore, and a bunny eats only plants.

clue.text: Swamp I sense may get sticky

parts.note: to glut is to swamp or flood with too much
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A boggy marsh feels as if it might turn gluey underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' reads as a bog, but it is a verb meaning overload.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutinous means gluey and adhesive, a direct synonym of sticky.

clue.text: Nasty mix of fuels found around coalmine?

indicators.note: found around means these mixed letters surround the mine word
mix of means the letters of the fuel word are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A dangerous blend of fuels at a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled fuel letters split either side of the mine, with one letter before it and four after.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful person is malicious and mean, which is nasty.

clue.text: Oral stimulants that get the team going?

definitions.text: Oral stimulants that get the team going?

parts.words: Oral stimulants that get the team going?
parts.note: sounds like drugs taken by mouth, but the stimulus is a rousing speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral stimulants' suggests pills or doping; it means spoken encouragement, the kind a coach gives in the dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousing speeches from a captain or coach are spoken words meant to motivate players before a match.

clue.text: Special time? I'll make up a rhyme

definitions.text: Special time? I'll make up a rhyme

parts.words: Special time? I'll make up a rhyme
parts.note: the speaker is the official court poet, who writes verses for royal and national occasions

explanation.walkthrough: The holder of this British post is expected to compose poems for special events such as coronations and royal weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: The national poet appointed by the monarch writes celebratory verse whenever there is a grand occasion.

clue.text: Cancel Tyneside opening

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A new venue in the North East has its opening called off.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to nullify or invalidate it, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: Lawyer's clothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the case papers given to a barrister are ...

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about what a lawyer wears; split it into the lawyer's case papers and an item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister receives written instructions called briefs, and the same word names short underpants.

clue.text: Announced paired couples, part of dance ensemble

indicators.note: announced means the words are spoken aloud, so we want a word that sounds like them

parts.note: two couples, each a two, side by side make two-two

explanation.surface: A caller at a dance names the pairings for a group number.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff skirt is one item of the costume worn when dancing ballet.

clue.text: Drink, awfully big and green, set before Queen

indicators.note: set before places the jumbled letters ahead of the royal abbreviation
awfully suggests the words are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A huge, sickly green beverage is placed in front of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fizzy non-alcoholic or lightly brewed beverage flavoured with the root spice.

clue.text: Dope sits on middle of road somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue sits on means the first piece lies above, so before, the next

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope

indicators.note: middle of means only the central pair of letters of the next word is kept

parts.note: the central letters of road

explanation.surface: A drugged person slumps in the middle of a road in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' means drugs on the surface, but it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major port city on Italy's north-west coast.

clue.text: Talented, topped chart

indicators.note: topped means having its head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a table is a chart of figures

explanation.surface: A gifted performer went to number one in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped chart' reads as reaching number one; here it means the word for chart loses its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An able person is skilled and capable, which is close to talented.

clue.text: Total pleasure, hosting 50s bash

indicators.note: hosting means holding the other pieces inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: fun means pleasure
L is the Roman numeral for 50, so two of them are LL
a blow is a bash or hit

explanation.surface: A really enjoyable time at a party with a 1950s theme.
explanation.walkthrough: '50s' looks like a decade for the party; it is two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-blown means complete or fully developed, as in a full-blown crisis, so it is a synonym for total.

clue.text: Uncle Sam, for instance, rejected convention

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: eg (exempli gratia) means for instance

explanation.surface: An American official turns down an international agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convention' looks like a treaty the USA rejects; it is the definition, meaning custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or practice, which is what a convention is.

clue.text: Discussed coaching contracts

indicators.note: discussed means talked about out loud, so the word for coaching is heard rather than seen

parts.note: coaching is given in lessons

explanation.surface: Agents talked over the terms of a coaching deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a noun for deals, but here it is a verb meaning shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or make smaller, which is what something does when it lessens.

clue.text: Sprightly, making westward part of journey in southern sea

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means right to left, so the built string is read backwards
in puts the stage of the journey inside the sea

parts.note: taken as the word itself
a leg is one stage of a journey

explanation.surface: A lively traveller sails west on one stretch of a voyage through southern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue west is leftward, so 'making westward' turns the whole assembled string round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seems not to grow old stays lively and youthful, so sprightly fits.
